defmodule Outbox.Ledger.Account do
  @moduledoc """
  A ledger account.
  """

  use Ash.Resource,
    otp_app: :outbox,
    domain: Outbox.Ledger,
    data_layer: Ash.DataLayer.Ets

  ets do
    private? false
  end

  attributes do
    uuid_primary_key :id

    attribute :owner_id, :string, allow_nil?: false, public?: true
    attribute :name, :string, allow_nil?: false, public?: true
    attribute :balance, :integer, allow_nil?: false, default: 0, public?: true

    attribute :status, :atom,
      allow_nil?: false,
      default: :active,
      constraints: [one_of: [:active, :frozen, :closed]],
      public?: true
  end

  actions do
    defaults [:read]

    create :open do
      primary? true
      accept [:owner_id, :name, :balance]
    end

    update :rename do
      accept [:name]
    end

    update :freeze do
      accept []
      change set_attribute(:status, :frozen)
    end

    update :deposit do
      accept []
      argument :amount, :integer, allow_nil?: false
      change atomic_update(:balance, expr(balance + ^arg(:amount)))
    end

    update :withdraw do
      require_atomic? false
      accept []
      argument :amount, :integer, allow_nil?: false
      validate {Outbox.Ledger.SufficientFunds, []}
      change atomic_update(:balance, expr(balance - ^arg(:amount)))
    end

    destroy :close do
      primary? true
    end
  end
end

defmodule Outbox.Ledger.SufficientFunds do
  @moduledoc """
  Rejects a withdrawal that is not positive or that would overdraw the account.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Validation

  @impl true
  def validate(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    amount = Ash.Changeset.get_argument(changeset, :amount)

    cond do
      not is_integer(amount) or amount <= 0 ->
        {:error,
         Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidArgument.exception(
           field: :amount,
           message: "must be positive"
         )}

      amount > changeset.data.balance ->
        {:error,
         Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidArgument.exception(
           field: :amount,
           message: "insufficient funds"
         )}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end
end

defmodule Ash.Reactor.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Reactor middleware used to collect and emit notifications upon successful
  completion of the Reactor.
  """

  use Reactor.Middleware

  require Logger

  @agent_key :ash_notification_agent
  @notification_key :ash_notifications

  defguardp has_agent?(context)
            when is_map_key(context, @agent_key) and
                   :erlang.map_get(@agent_key, context) != []

  defguardp has_notifications?(context)
            when is_map_key(context, @notification_key) and
                   :erlang.map_get(@notification_key, context) != []

  @doc """
  When starting a reactor, start an agent to act as a temporary store of
  notifications.
  """
  @impl true
  def init(context) when has_notifications?(context) do
    with {:ok, notifications} <- Map.fetch(context, @notification_key),
         {:ok, context} <- agent_start(context),
         {:ok, context} <- agent_put(context, notifications) do
      context =
        context
        |> Map.delete(@notification_key)

      {:ok, context}
    end
  end

  def init(context), do: agent_start(context)

  @doc """
  When halting the reactor, store any queued notifications in the context for
  eventual resumption.
  """
  @impl true
  def halt(context) when has_agent?(context) do
    with {:ok, notifications} <- agent_get(context),
         {:ok, context} <- agent_stop(context) do
      if Enum.any?(notifications) do
        {:ok,
         Map.update(
           context,
           @notification_key,
           notifications,
           &Enum.concat(&1, notifications)
         )}
      else
        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When the reactor completes successfully, publish any queued notifications.
  """
  @impl true
  def complete(result, context) when has_agent?(context) do
    with {:ok, notifications} <- agent_get(context),
         {:ok, context} <- agent_stop(context),
         [] <- __MODULE__.publish(context, notifications) do
      {:ok, result}
    else
      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}

      notifications when is_list(notifications) ->
        if Process.get(:ash_started_transaction?) do
          Process.put(
            :ash_notifications,
            List.wrap(Process.get(:ash_notifications)) ++
              notifications
          )
        else
          {:current_stacktrace, stacktrace} = Process.info(self(), :current_stacktrace)

          Logger.warning("""
            Missed #{Enum.count(notifications)} notifications in Reactor complete hook.

            This happens when your steps return notifications but they are unable to be published
            upon successful completion of the reactor.

            #{Exception.format_stacktrace(stacktrace)}
          """)
        end

        {:ok, result}
    end
  end

  def complete(result, _context), do: {:ok, result}

  @doc """
  When the reactor fails, discard any queued notifications.
  """
  @impl true
  def error(_errors, context) do
    agent_stop(context)

    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Add notifications to the queue to be published on reactor success.
  """
  @spec enqueue_notifications(Reactor.context(), Enumerable.t(Ash.Notifier.Notification.t())) ::
          :ok | {:error, any}
  def enqueue_notifications(context, notifications) do
    with {:ok, _} <- agent_put(context, notifications) do
      :ok
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Dispatch notifications.
  """
  @spec publish(
          Reactor.context(),
          Ash.Notifier.Notification.t() | [Ash.Notifier.Notification.t()]
        ) ::
          [Ash.Notifier.Notification.t()]
  def publish(context, notifications) when has_agent?(context) do
    case agent_put(context, notifications) do
      {:ok, _} -> []
      {:error, _} -> notifications
    end
  end

  def publish(_, notifications), do: Ash.Notifier.notify(notifications)

  defp agent_start(context) do
    case Agent.start_link(fn -> [] end) do
      {:ok, pid} -> {:ok, Map.update(context, @agent_key, [pid], &[pid | &1])}
      {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp agent_get(%{@agent_key => [pid | _]}) do
    notifications = Agent.get(pid, & &1, 100)
    {:ok, notifications}
  rescue
    error -> {:error, error}
  end

  defp agent_stop(%{@agent_key => [pid | agents]} = context) do
    :ok = Agent.stop(pid, :normal)

    {:ok, %{context | @agent_key => agents}}
  rescue
    error -> {:error, error}
  end

  defp agent_put(%{@agent_key => [pid | _]} = context, notifications) do
    :ok = Agent.update(pid, &Enum.concat(&1, notifications))

    {:ok, context}
  rescue
    error -> {:error, error}
  end
end

defmodule Outbox.Eventing.Counters do
  @moduledoc """
  Atomic counters for outbox sequence numbers.
  """

  @table :outbox_counters

  def init do
    case :ets.whereis(@table) do
      :undefined ->
        :ets.new(@table, [:set, :named_table, :public, write_concurrency: true])
        :ets.insert(@table, {:global_sequence, 0})
        :ok

      _ ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def increment_global do
    :ets.update_counter(@table, :global_sequence, 1, {:global_sequence, 0})
  end

  def increment_aggregate(type, id) do
    :ets.update_counter(@table, {:aggregate_sequence, type, id}, 1, {{:aggregate_sequence, type, id}, 0})
  end

  def reset do
    # Clear everything.
    :ets.delete_all_objects(@table)
    :ets.insert(@table, {:global_sequence, 0})
    :ok
  end

  # For testing/replay
  def current_global do
    case :ets.lookup(@table, :global_sequence) do
      [{_, v}] -> v
      [] -> 0
    end
  end
end

defmodule Outbox.Eventing.Notifier do
  @moduledoc """
  Captures successful writes to ledger resources and writes them to the outbox.
  """

  use Ash.Notifier

  require Logger

  @impl true
  def notify(notification) do
    # We only care about create, update, and destroy actions on ledger resources.
    # Reads never produce entries.
    if ledger_resource?(notification.resource) do
      handle_notification(notification)
    end
  end

  defp ledger_resource?(resource) when is_atom(resource) do
    case Module.split(resource) do
      ["Outbox", "Ledger", _] -> true
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp ledger_resource?(_), do: false

  defp handle_notification(notification) do
    resource_module = notification.resource
    action_name = notification.action.name

    # Topic: ledger.<aggregate_type>.<action_name>
    aggregate_type = resource_module |> Module.split() |> List.last() |> Macro.underscore()
    topic = "ledger.#{aggregate_type}.#{action_name}"

    # Record and aggregate_id
    record = notification.data
    aggregate_id = record.id

    # Actor
    actor_id =
      case Map.get(notification, :actor) do
        %{id: id} when is_binary(id) -> id
        _ -> nil
      end

    # Changes
    changes = changes_map(notification)

    # Global and aggregate sequences
    global_seq = Outbox.Eventing.Counters.increment_global()
    agg_seq = Outbox.Eventing.Counters.increment_aggregate(aggregate_type, aggregate_id)

    # Dedup key: <aggregate_type>:<aggregate_id>:<action>:<aggregate_sequence>
    dedup_key = "#{aggregate_type}:#{aggregate_id}:#{action_name}:#{agg_seq}"

    # Write to outbox. Since it's ETS data layer and we're in the same app,
    # we can just use the resource's create action. The dedup_key identity ensures
    # a duplicate entry can't be stored. If insertion fails (duplicate), we ignore
    # it since that would mean the notification was already processed. But it's
    # a single write producing exactly one entry, so it should be fine. Actually,
    # if the action is retried, we could get another. We should accept and just
    # ignore if unique constraint violated.

    _ = Outbox.Eventing.Event.create(%{
      sequence: global_seq,
      aggregate_sequence: agg_seq,
      topic: topic,
      resource: resource_module |> Module.split() |> Enum.join("."),
      aggregate_type: aggregate_type,
      aggregate_id: aggregate_id,
      action: action_name,
      actor_id: actor_id,
      changes: changes,
      dedup_key: dedup_key
    }, domain: Outbox.Eventing)

    :ok
  end

  defp changes_map(notification) do
    changeset = notification.changeset

    case notification.action.type do
      :create ->
        # Every public, non-primary-key attribute with non-nil value, from nil.
        attrs = Ash.Resource.Info.attributes(notification.resource)
        pkey = Ash.Resource.Info.primary_key(notification.resource)
        record = notification.data

        Enum.reduce(attrs, %{}, fn attr, acc ->
          if attr.public? and attr.name not in pkey do
            val = Map.get(record, attr.name)
            if not is_nil(val) do
              Map.put(acc, Atom.to_string(attr.name), %{"from" => nil, "to" => encode(val)})
            else
              acc
            end
          else
            acc
          end
        end)

      :update ->
        # Attributes that actually differ, from before to after.
        # Ash provides the before record in notification.data in non-batch? Not
        # quite. For update, data is the record before. We can also get the after
        # record from the changeset results or by applying the changes to the data.
        attrs = Ash.Resource.Info.attributes(notification.resource)
        pkey = Ash.Resource.Info.primary_key(notification.resource)
        pre_record = notification.data
        post_record = changeset.data

        Enum.reduce(attrs, %{}, fn attr, acc ->
          if attr.public? and attr.name not in pkey do
            from = encode(Map.get(pre_record, attr.name))
            to = encode(Map.get(post_record, attr.name))
            if from != to do
              Map.put(acc, Atom.to_string(attr.name), %{"from" => from, "to" => to})
            else
              acc
            end
          else
            acc
          end
        end)

      :destroy ->
        %{}

      _ ->
        %{}
    end
  end

  defp encode(nil), do: nil
  defp encode(a) when is_atom(a), do: Atom.to_string(a)
  defp encode(v), do: v
end

defmodule Outbox.Eventing.Notifier do
  @moduledoc """
  Captures successful writes to ledger resources and writes them to the outbox.
  """

  use Ash.Notifier

  require Logger

  @impl true
  def notify(notification) do
    # We only care about create, update, and destroy actions on ledger resources.
    # Reads never produce entries.
    if ledger_resource?(notification.resource) do
      handle_notification(notification)
    end
  end

  defp ledger_resource?(resource) when is_atom(resource) do
    case Module.split(resource) do
      ["Outbox", "Ledger", _] -> true
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp ledger_resource?(_), do: false

  defp handle_notification(notification) do
    resource_module = notification.resource
    action_name = notification.action.name

    # Topic: ledger.<aggregate_type>.<action_name>
    aggregate_type = resource_module |> Module.split() |> List.last() |> Macro.underscore()
    topic = "ledger.#{aggregate_type}.#{action_name}"

    # Record and aggregate_id
    record = notification.data
    aggregate_id = record.id

    # Actor
    actor_id =
      case Map.get(notification, :actor) do
        %{id: id} when is_binary(id) -> id
        _ -> nil
      end

    # Changes
    changes = changes_map(notification)

    # Global and aggregate sequences
    global_seq = Outbox.Eventing.Counters.increment_global()
    agg_seq = Outbox.Eventing.Counters.increment_aggregate(aggregate_type, aggregate_id)

    # Dedup key: <aggregate_type>:<aggregate_id>:<action>:<aggregate_sequence>
    dedup_key = "#{aggregate_type}:#{aggregate_id}:#{action_name}:#{agg_seq}"

    # Write to outbox. Since it's ETS data layer and we're in the same app,
    # we can use the domain's create action. The dedup_key identity ensures a
    # duplicate entry can't be stored. If insertion fails (duplicate), we ignore
    # it since that would mean the notification was already processed. But it's
    # a single write producing exactly one entry, so it should be fine. Actually,
    # if the action is retried, we could get another. We should accept and just
    # ignore if unique constraint violated.

    _ = Outbox.Eventing.create(%{
      sequence: global_seq,
      aggregate_sequence: agg_seq,
      topic: topic,
      resource: resource_module |> Module.split() |> Enum.join("."),
      aggregate_type: aggregate_type,
      aggregate_id: aggregate_id,
      action: action_name,
      actor_id: actor_id,
      changes: changes,
      dedup_key: dedup_key
    })

    :ok
  end

  defp changes_map(notification) do
    changeset = notification.changeset

    case notification.action.type do
      :create ->
        # Every public, non-primary-key attribute with non-nil value, from nil.
        attrs = Ash.Resource.Info.attributes(notification.resource)
        pkey = Ash.Resource.Info.primary_key(notification.resource)
        record = notification.data

        Enum.reduce(attrs, %{}, fn attr, acc ->
          if attr.public? and attr.name not in pkey do
            val = Map.get(record, attr.name)
            if not is_nil(val) do
              Map.put(acc, Atom.to_string(attr.name), %{"from" => nil, "to" => encode(val)})
            else
              acc
            end
          else
            acc
          end
        end)

      :update ->
        # Attributes that actually differ, from before to after.
        # Ash provides the before record in notification.data in non-batch? Not
        # quite. For update, data is the record before. We can also get the after
        # record from the changeset results or by applying the changes to the data.
        attrs = Ash.Resource.Info.attributes(notification.resource)
        pkey = Ash.Resource.Info.primary_key(notification.resource)
        pre_record = notification.data
        post_record = changeset.data

        Enum.reduce(attrs, %{}, fn attr, acc ->
          if attr.public? and attr.name not in pkey do
            from = encode(Map.get(pre_record, attr.name))
            to = encode(Map.get(post_record, attr.name))
            if from != to do
              Map.put(acc, Atom.to_string(attr.name), %{"from" => from, "to" => to})
            else
              acc
            end
          else
            acc
          end
        end)

      :destroy ->
        %{}

      _ ->
        %{}
    end
  end

  defp encode(nil), do: nil
  defp encode(a) when is_atom(a), do: Atom.to_string(a)
  defp encode(v), do: v
end

defmodule Outbox.Eventing.Dispatcher do
  @moduledoc """
  A local dispatcher process that fans out outbox entries to subscribers.
  """

  use GenServer

  @name __MODULE__

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: @name)
  end

  def subscribe(id, pattern, handler, opts \\ []) do
    mode = Keyword.get(opts, :mode, :async)
    GenServer.call(@name, {:subscribe, id, pattern, handler, mode})
  end

  def unsubscribe(id) do
    GenServer.cast(@name, {:unsubscribe, id})
  end

  def flush do
    GenServer.call(@name, :flush, :infinity)
  end

  def dead_letters do
    GenServer.call(@name, :dead_letters)
  end

  def reset do
    GenServer.call(@name, :reset)
  end

  def deliver_sync(entry) do
    GenServer.call(@name, {:deliver_sync, entry})
  end

  def notify_entry(entry) do
    GenServer.cast(@name, {:notify_entry, entry})
  end

  def replay(after_sequence, subscriber_id) do
    GenServer.call(@name, {:replay, after_sequence, subscriber_id})
  end

  @impl true
  def init(_opts) do
    {:ok, initial_state()}
  end

  defp initial_state do
    %{
      subscribers: [], # {id, pattern, handler, mode}
      pending: [],     # {subscriber_id, entry, attempts}
      dead_letters: [], # {subscriber_id, sequence, attempts, reason}
      last_seen: 0
    }
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:subscribe, id, pattern, handler, mode}, _from, state) do
    if Enum.any?(state.subscribers, fn {s_id, _, _, _} -> s_id == id end) do
      {:reply, {:error, :already_subscribed}, state}
    else
      s = {id, pattern, handler, mode}
      {:reply, :ok, %{state | subscribers: state.subscribers ++ [s]}}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_cast({:unsubscribe, id}, state) do
    subs = Enum.reject(state.subscribers, fn {s_id, _, _, _} -> s_id == id end)
    pending = Enum.reject(state.pending, fn {s_id, _, _} -> s_id == id end)
    {:noreply, %{state | subscribers: subs, pending: pending}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_cast({:notify_entry, entry}, state) do
    last_seen = max(state.last_seen, entry.sequence)
    {:noreply, %{state | last_seen: last_seen}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call(:flush, _from, state) do
    state = fetch_new_entries(state)
    {pending, dead} = drain(state.pending, state.subscribers)
    {:reply, :ok, %{state | pending: pending, dead_letters: state.dead_letters ++ dead}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call(:dead_letters, _from, state) do
    dl = Enum.sort_by(state.dead_letters, fn {s_id, seq, _attempts, _reason} ->
      idx = Enum.find_index(state.subscribers, fn {id, _, _, _} -> id == s_id end)
      idx = if idx == nil, do: 99999, else: idx
      {seq, idx}
    end)

    formatted = Enum.map(dl, fn {s_id, seq, attempts, reason} ->
      %{subscriber_id: s_id, sequence: seq, attempts: attempts, reason: reason}
    end)

    {:reply, formatted, state}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call(:reset, _from, _state) do
    Outbox.Eventing.Counters.reset()
    Outbox.Eventing.delete_all()
    {:reply, :ok, initial_state()}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:deliver_sync, entry}, _from, state) do
    {pending, dead} = sync_deliver(entry, state.subscribers, state.pending)
    {:reply, :ok, %{state | pending: pending, dead_letters: state.dead_letters ++ dead}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:replay, seq, s_id}, _from, state) do
    subs = Enum.find(state.subscribers, fn {id, _, _, _} -> id == s_id end)
    if subs do
      {_id, pattern, handler, _} = subs
      events = Outbox.Eventing.list_events!()
      after_events = Enum.filter(events, fn e -> e.sequence > seq end)

      delivered = Enum.flat_map(after_events, fn e ->
        if topic_matches?(e.topic, pattern) do
          case handler.(e) do
            :ok -> [e.sequence]
            {:error, _} -> []
          end
        else
          []
        end
      end)
      {:reply, {:ok, delivered}, state}
    else
      {:reply, {:ok, []}, state}
    end
  end

  # -- Drain logic --

  defp fetch_new_entries(state) do
    all = Outbox.Eventing.list_events!()
    new = Enum.filter(all, fn e -> e.sequence > state.last_seen end)

    pending =
      Enum.flat_map(new, fn e ->
        Enum.map(state.subscribers, fn {s_id, pattern, _, _} ->
          if topic_matches?(e.topic, pattern) do
            {s_id, e, 0}
          else
            nil
          end
        end)
      end)
      |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)

    %{state | pending: state.pending ++ pending, last_seen: max(state.last_seen, Enum.reduce(new, state.last_seen, &max(&1.sequence, &2)))}
  end

  defp drain(pending, subscribers) do
    # Attempt each pending delivery in ascending sequence order.
    # For equal sequence, order by subscriber registration.
    sorted_pending = Enum.sort_by(pending, fn {s_id, entry, _attempts} ->
      idx = Enum.find_index(subscribers, fn {id, _, _, _} -> id == s_id end)
      idx = if idx == nil, do: 99999, else: idx
      {entry.sequence, idx}
    end)

    Enum.reduce(sorted_pending, {[], []}, fn delivery, {pending_acc, dead_acc} ->
      {s_id, entry, attempts} = delivery
      subs = Enum.find(subscribers, fn {id, _, _, _} -> id == s_id end)

      if subs do
        {_, _, handler, _} = subs

        case try_deliver(handler, entry) do
          :ok ->
            {pending_acc, dead_acc}

          {:error, reason} ->
            attempts = attempts + 1
            if attempts >= 3 do
              {pending_acc, dead_acc ++ [{s_id, entry.sequence, attempts, reason}]}
            else
              {pending_acc ++ [{s_id, entry, attempts}], dead_acc}
            end
        end
      else
        {pending_acc, dead_acc}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp sync_deliver(entry, subscribers, pending) do
    Enum.reduce(subscribers, {pending, []}, fn {s_id, pattern, handler, mode}, {p_acc, d_acc} ->
      if topic_matches?(entry.topic, pattern) do
        # If :async, don't deliver here; it joins pending.
        # If :sync, deliver.
        if mode == :sync do
          case try_deliver(handler, entry) do
            :ok -> {p_acc, d_acc}
            {:error, reason} ->
              # Count as first attempt.
              attempts = 1
              if attempts >= 3 do
                {p_acc, d_acc ++ [{s_id, entry.sequence, attempts, reason}]}
              else
                {p_acc ++ [{s_id, entry, attempts}], d_acc}
              end
          end
        else
          # :async joins pending as a new delivery (attempts=0).
          {p_acc ++ [{s_id, entry, 0}], d_acc}
        end
      else
        {p_acc, d_acc}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp try_deliver(handler, entry) do
    try do
      case handler.(entry) do
        :ok -> :ok
        {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
      end
    rescue
      e -> {:error, {:raised, Exception.message(e)}}
    end
  end

  # -- Topic matching --

  defp topic_matches?(topic, pattern) do
    topic_segs = String.split(topic, ".")
    pat_segs = String.split(pattern, ".")

    match_segs?(topic_segs, pat_segs)
  end

  defp match_segs?([], []), do: true
  defp match_segs?(_, []), do: false

  defp match_segs?(ts, ["#"]), do: true
  defp match_segs?([_ | ts], ["*"]), do: match_segs?(ts, [])
  defp match_segs?([t | ts], [p | ps]) do
    case p do
      "*" -> match_segs?(ts, ps)
      lit -> if t == lit, do: match_segs?(ts, ps), else: false
    end
  end
  defp match_segs?([], _), do: false
end
